content: It appears to be a comprehensive list of treatment regimens for various infections, including gastrointestinal, intra-abdominal, biliary, and others. Gastrointestinal and Intra-abdominal Infections Anthrax, Gastrointestinal 1. Preferred Regimen (1): Administer ciprofloxacin 400 mg intravenously (IV) every 8 hours (q8h) in combination with clindamycin 600 mg IV q8h. 2. Preferred Regimen (2): Administer ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h in combination with penicillin G 4 million units (MU) every 4–6 hours. 3. Preferred Regimen (3): Administer ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h in combination with meropenem 1 g IV every 6–8 hours. 4. Preferred Regimen (4): Administer ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h in combination with rifampin 300 mg every 12 hours (q12h). 5. Preferred Regimen (5): Administer doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h in combination with clindamycin 600 mg IV q8h. 6. Preferred Regimen (6): Administer doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h in combination with penicillin G 4 MU every 4–6 hours. 7. Preferred Regimen (7): Administer doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h in combination with meropenem 1 g IV every 6–8 hours. 8. Preferred Regimen (8): Administer doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h in combination with rifampin 300 mg q12h. Note: Treatment duration of 60 days is recommended to prevent relapse or breakthrough of incubating disease. If initial therapy is intravenous, transition to oral administration (ciprofloxacin or doxycycline) when clinically indicated. Steroids may be considered as adjunct therapy for patients with severe edema or meningitis. For pregnant women, avoid doxycycline; instead, use ciprofloxacin and switch to oral penicillin once susceptibilities are known. Appendicitis 1. Community-acquired infection in adults: Mild-to-moderate severity (e.g., perforated or abscessed appendicitis): Single-agent regimens: 1. Cefotetan 2 g IV q6h. 2. Ertapenem 1 g IV q24h. 3. Moxifloxacin 400 mg IV q24h. 4. Tigecycline 100 mg initial dose, then 50 mg IV q12h. 5. Ticarcillin-clavulanic acid 3.1 g IV q6h (FDA labeling indicates 200 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 6 hours for moderate infections). Combination regimens: 1. Cefazolin 1–2 g IV q8h AND metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h OR 1500 mg q24h. 2. Cefuroxime 1.5 g IV q8h AND metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h OR 1500 mg q24h. 3. Ceftriaxone 1–2 g IV q12–24h AND metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h OR 1500 mg q24h. 4. Cefotaxime 1–2 g IV q6–8h AND metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h OR 1500 mg q24h. 5. Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h AND metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h OR 1500 mg q24h. 6. Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h AND metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h OR 1500 mg q24h. High-risk or severe cases (e.g., severe physiologic disturbance, advanced age, or immunocompromised state): Single-agent regimens: 1. Imipenem-cilastatin 500 mg IV q6h OR 1 g q8h. 2. Meropenem 1 g IV q8h. 3. Doripenem 500 mg IV q8h. 4. Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 g IV q6h. Combination regimens: 1. Cefepime 2 g IV q8–12h AND metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h OR 1500 mg q24h. 2. Ceftazidime 2 g IV q8h AND metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h OR 1500 mg q24h. 3. Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h AND metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h OR 1500 mg q24h. 4. Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h AND metronidazole 500 mg IV q8–12h OR 1500 mg q24h. Note: Antimicrobial therapy for established infections should be limited to 4–7 days unless achieving adequate source control is difficult. Longer durations of therapy have not been associated with improved outcomes.
